items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: They were Gus McClung, Henry Goodwin and Residus 'Mac' Horton, three members of Cooper's orchestra... I had not played with the other members but knew them and they were... Henry Goodwin... and myself.

ctx.x: I had been out drinking most of the Tuesday night that week when Ralph was at the Lafayette and could sleep late on Wednesday. Russell had a dance to play Wednesday night in a hall up over the Alhambra Theater at 7th Avenue and 126th Street.

I was deep in slumberland when someone knocked on my door about 12.30 in the afternoon. It was the landlady of the rooming house where I was staying on 135th Street. My wife was working as a housemaid down town so I could sleep the whole day, so I had thought when I came home. The landlady told me that three men were at the hall door and wanted to see me. I told her to let them in. They were Gus McClung, Henry Goodwin and Residus 'Mac' Horton, three members of Cooper's orchestra. I had known Gus since the first…

They told me that the other trumpet player whose name was Louis Hunt was having lip trouble and felt so embarrassed because he had a feature number to do and had been missing the ending for a few days. So he did not show up for the first show and they had come to ask me if I would come to the theater and be on hand to do the next show if Hunt did not appear. I was so beat and knowing that I had to work with Russel that night, I told them I could not make it.
